newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh Uzen oil tender result seen by end March.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh Uzen oil tender result seen by end March.

text.p: The Kazakh government will announce the winner of an international tender for the right to develop the giant Uzen oilfield by the end of March, a senior official told reporters late on Monday.

Sarybay Kalmurzayev, head of the State Property Committee, said that the country's Oil and Gas Ministry -- transformed last week into the national Kazakh Oil company -- had delayed the sale's results.
"They (the Oil and Gas Ministry) have upset the tender, and we have been ordered to finalise the work," Kalmurzayev said.
Amoco Corp of the United States, Malaysian state oil firm Petronas and China National Petroleum Corp (CNPC) are the finalists.
Development of Uzen, Kazakhstan's second largest oilfield after Tengiz, with estimated reserves of around 150 million tonnes of oil, will cost around $1.2 billion.
Work on Uzen was launched in 1965, and the Oil & Gas in Kazakhstan magazine said around 260 million tonnes of oil had been extracted over the last three decades.
Uzen's oil output peaked at 16 million tonnes in 1975 but fell to nine million tonnes by 1980. Oil output in recent years has shrunk 20 percent annually.

Balgimbayev has said investment in Uzen, located 150 km (100 miles) east of the Caspian Sea in southwest Kazakhstan, would raise the field's current output of 2.7 million tonnes a year to about seven million tonnes.
